gloss: all of them; every one; any of them

definitions.explanation: Refers to every item in a group without exception, emphasizing that the same quality or condition applies to each one.

examples.japanese: どれも{同|おな}じに{見|み}える。
examples.english: They all look the same to me.

examples.japanese: {商品|しょうひん}はどれも{品質|ひんしつ}が{高|たか}いので、{安心|あんしん}して{買|か}えます。
examples.english: All the products are high quality, so you can buy them with confidence.

notes:
Combines the interrogative pronoun どれ (which one) with the inclusive particle も to mean "all of them" or "every single one." Used when referring to multiple items or options and indicating that the same judgment applies to each.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- どれも〜ない: none of them (with negative verb)
- どれも{同|おな}じ: they're all the same
- どれもこれも: each and every one (emphatic)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- どれも{美味|おい}しい: they're all delicious
- どれも{素晴|すば}らしい: they're all wonderful
- どれも{気|き}に{入|い}らない: I don't like any of them

SIMILAR WORDS:
- どちらも: both (used for two items)
- どれでも: any one of them / whichever (implies choosing one)
- {全部|ぜんぶ}: all, everything — more general; どれも emphasizes individual items within a visible group
